bundler_status.cause: comparison/llm.py derives each pair's expected provider-call topology from the shared execution map, which declares a relation_nature sub-call for 17,235 of 33,361 pairs. The verdict-only substrate removed that call, so every [Complex] pair mismatches and all four arms are rejected at their first one.
bundler_status.consequence: The verdict-only side carries no bundle digest. Its statement probabilities are computed here, by the same statement_belief entry point and the same priors, and the thinking side is recomputed alongside it and gated against the shipped bundle so both sides are known to come from one code path.

bootstrap.design: paired statement bootstrap, stratified independently within each frozen fold while preserving its size, one shared index vector across every arm and both sides

error_class.decision_rule: flag a statement as an ERROR iff belief < tau
error_class.deployed_cut_rule: both sides cut at the DELIBERATING side's own tau -- what a curator who swapped the model and left the cutoff alone would get. No oracle is available to the verdict-only side under this rule.
error_class.headline: error-class F1 is the metric /paper leads on: the panel is 73.2% positive, so ranking measures barely move while error catching does
error_class.oracle_disclosure: Every tau here is chosen ON THIS PANEL, with these labels already in hand, to maximise the arm's OWN error-class F1. It is fitted AND evaluated on the same 1689 statements, it would not be available before curation, and no cut here is validated out of sample. That is an ORACLE, and it FAVOURS the paper's RF rather than us: the RF's near-continuous scores give the search 1546 candidate cuts to optimise over, where the three reader arms that win have 475-498 and Gemma 4 E2B gate has 420. The side handed the finest-grained oracle still loses by +0.1416 to GLM-5 gate. Read this as an operating-point comparison, not as a held-out result. It covers the headline cut ONLY; the matched_recall block's second cut is fitted on this panel too, by a different rule, and is disclosed separately in matched_recall_rule.
error_class.threshold_rule: tau is the arm's OWN full-panel best-error-F1 cut: of the arm's own distinct scores, the one whose flag set {belief < tau} maximises error-class F1 on all 1689 statements. Ties are broken to the SMALLEST such cut, so the rule is a function of the score vector alone and does not depend on the order the rows arrived in. Each arm is cut at its own tau; no cut is shared and none is transferred between arms.
